title: Six-Second Counter-Pressing Rule
definition: A tactical protocol requiring the team to immediately swarm the ball carrier for six seconds after losing possession to regain it before the opponent can organize.
content: This concept addresses the vulnerability created by high-possession teams that maintain short distances between players to retain the ball. When possession is lost, these compact structures leave defenders close to the ball, creating an immediate opportunity for recovery. The 'six-second rule' dictates that the team must exert intense, unrelenting pressure on the ball carrier for exactly six seconds. This high-intensity counter-press aims to disrupt the opponent's initial build-up and force a turnover before they can establish a stable shape. If the ball is not recovered within this window, the team must immediately transition into a pre-defined compact defensive shape, such as a 4-1-4-1, to protect the goal and prepare for the next phase. This approach prevents the opponent from exploiting the space behind the high defensive line and neutralizes the threat of quick counter-attacks by opponents who sit deep. It transforms the defensive transition from a reactive scramble into a structured, time-bound tactical action that maximizes the numerical advantage present near the point of loss.
example_questions: How long should we press aggressively after losing the ball before we fall back into our defensive shape?
We just lost possession in midfield and the opponent has time to set up a counter-attack, what should the nearest player do immediately?
As a midfielder, what is my specific job in the first few seconds after the team loses the ball in the attacking third?
We keep getting caught out of position because we don't recover the ball quickly enough, what is the standard protocol for immediate recovery?
